movement_profile.difficulty: Intermediate (due to fast footwork and ribbon tying)
movement_profile.footwork: Intricate zapateado emphasizing right heel stamping; fast and precise
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Couples dancing together, sometimes multiple couples; spatially centered around ribbon tying
movement_profile.partnering: Couples perform coordinated footwork and ribbon tying
movement_profile.posture: Straight and erect, similar to Irish jig dancers

signature_moves.description: Couples use their feet to tie a large ribbon into a lover's knot on the dance floor, symbolizing union.
signature_moves.name: Ribbon Knot Tying

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Fast binary rhythm, lively and energetic
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid insulting improvised lyrics in social settings to prevent conflicts

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Ostinato arpeggiated pattern supporting zapateado footwork
music_profile.sound_description: Bright harp arpeggios intertwine with rhythmic guitar strumming and lively vocals, driven by a fast, binary rhythm that mirrors the dancers’ energetic footwork.

basic_steps: Begin with slow stamping of right heel (zapateado)
Increase tempo to fast binary rhythm
Perform intricate footwork emphasizing heel taps
Use feet to tie a ribbon into a knot on the floor
Toss the ribbon knot into the air to finish
teaching.formation: Couples (traditionally one man and one woman), sometimes multiple couples
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with basic heel stamping and posture; advanced dancers perform fast zapateado and ribbon tying
teaching.rhythm: Fast binary meter with ostinato pattern
